## Published release

**v0.3.0** was published on 22 May 2026. Its release page currently provides
one `amd64.deb` package. It predates the recent changes listed below;
do not assume that an installed binary reporting `0.3.0` includes them.

See the [release assets](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/projcli/releases/tag/v0.3.0)
and [installation status](install.qmd). A new release and repaired installers
are being prepared.

## On main: development preview

These capabilities are implemented on `main`. They are not a claim about the
older published package.

| Capability | What it means for you |
|---|---|
| Choose the project | `--project PATH` selects the folder for a command. Child queries retain that root. |
| Preview an analysis | `build-dev` runs your selected steps without CLI version changes, output promotion or archive export. |
| Read without changing files | Configuration validation and path queries do not create target folders or edit ignore files. |
| Detect command failures | Errors produce a nonzero exit status, so an automated run can stop. |
| Run without questions | `--non-interactive` disables CLI prompts and automatic package installation, and closes runner input. |
| Select no analysis | An explicit `scripts: []` runs no analysis scripts. Hooks may still run; production can export existing outputs. |
| Run scripts and render documents | The build engine supports Python, R, Quarto and R Markdown/Bookdown targets, with the corresponding tools installed. |
| Keep a local output archive | Production builds can export configured outputs to local content-addressed storage, which avoids storing identical content repeatedly. |

### Preview has a boundary

The CLI skips its own release operations during a preview, including cleanup
of released outputs and prior caches. **This is not a filesystem sandbox.**
Scripts, hooks and renderers can still change files. Write preview results
to an explicitly chosen temporary folder, as in the [tutorial](tutorial.qmd).

Document renderers have their own working folders and output rules.
Mixed-language scheduling is not a promise that every target runs in the exact
order written in configuration. See the [build reference](cli/build.qmd) for
the current implementation and the [behavior contract](behavior.qmd) for limits.

## Still ahead

The broader project-root and build workflow milestones remain incomplete.
Do not rely on the following as established behavior:

- Matching results and paths across CLI runs, RStudio and GUI rendering.
- Full compatibility with every `projr` workflow.
- A released installer for every operating system and processor.
- A filesystem sandbox or automatic redirection of every renderer's output.
- Complete sequential ordering across mixed script and document targets.

The existing R package is unchanged. A Rust library is available in this
repository, but new R, Python and Julia frontend integrations are separate work.

For the detailed evidence and decisions, see the
[behavior contract](behavior.qmd) and [compatibility log](compatibility.qmd).
